items.notes: Missing the core claim that Kubernetes topology-spread only influences placement and cannot guarantee post-removal balance or database consistency, so placement must be paired with an isolated fault test of compute, identity and storage loss; the required evidence anchor for that claim is uncited.

All five core claims are substantively covered, with the only residual gap being the claim that out-of-order fixtures and measured output freshness are needed to test the declared lateness and correction policy; the failure-recovery-experiments anchor is uncited.

Missing the core claim distinguishing logical operation, transport attempt, resource, event and consumer-effect identities at their own durability boundaries, and the five-identities and retry-policy anchors are uncited.

Missing the core claim that search results leak through metadata such as counts, titles, snippets, related links and citations that must be filtered against the authorized subject and object, along with the no-mutation baseline for a read-only search surface.

Missing the core claim that backend errors or unknown failures must not be cached as absence and that the authorization path must fail closed and recheck changed state; the discriminating-failure-experiment and authority/data-contract anchors are uncited.
